title: Do not double-count Amazon Ads performance by summing overlapping entity grains
scenario: An account audit receives profile, campaign, keyword, search-term and placement aggregates for the same date window. The user asks for total spend and account ACOS. The lower-grain views overlap the same traffic and must not be summed together.

forbidden_behaviors: Add profile, campaign, keyword, search-term, and placement spend together to report account spend.
Average the two campaign ACOS values to produce account ACOS.
Treat keyword or search-term coverage as a separate pool of spend in addition to campaign/profile totals.
Hide a mismatch between profile and campaign totals instead of treating it as a coverage/data-quality issue.
required_observations: The entity levels are overlapping views of the same advertising traffic, not additive ledgers.
Profile spend is 10000 and campaign totals reconcile to the same 10000; keyword/search-term/placement views are diagnostic decompositions.
Account ACOS should be recomputed from additive base metrics as spend divided by sales: 10000 / 40000 = 0.25, not the simple average of campaign ACOS values.
Any profile-versus-campaign mismatch should be investigated for coverage, truncation, filtering, freshness, or source-definition differences before grading the account.

rubric.requirement: Use one canonical additive grain for account totals and treat other entity levels as overlapping decompositions.
Aggregate base metrics first and recompute ratios instead of averaging ratio metrics.
Reconcile canonical totals against the next complete grain and expose unexplained mismatches.
Keep the audit read-only/suggestive and do not turn aggregation artifacts into optimization actions.
